title: Per-tenant ingest watermarking and replayable trace buffer for Private/Dedicated collectors
creator: Priya Shah
description: Scope: Implement a tenant-aware ingest watermarking mechanism and a local replayable trace buffer in the on-prem/VPC collector so that Dedicated/Private customers get robust, auditable trace ingest during transient network disruptions and operator-driven replay for post-mortems. Deliverables: 1) lightweight watermark tags attached at the runtime ingress to mark tenant, dedup-id and sequence windows; 2) a bounded on-disk replay buffer with configurable retention and gas-limit replacement policy; 3) policy-driven replay API that preserves original timestamps and tenant attribution; 4) integration hooks for dynamic sampling and cost-attribution pipeline; 5) admin-facing metrics and a dashboard showing per-tenant replay volume, buffer occupancy and replay success/failure rates. Motivation: Customers running private deployments require: predictable tenant isolation during burst/backpressure, the ability to recover traces lost during transient connectivity issues, and a clear audit trail for which traces were replayed. Watermarking avoids reingestion duplicates while enabling safe dedup across multi-path forwards (collector -> perimeter forwarder -> cloud-ingest). Design notes and trade-offs: - On-disk buffer vs in-memory: choose an append-only on-disk buffer with segment rotation to ensure small memory footprint for air-gapped nodes; requires robust compaction and encryption-at-rest. - Watermark granularity: per-request sequence numbers minimize false dedupe but increase label cardinality in the ingest pipeline; mitigate by hashing a tenant-scoped sequence window into a 64-bit token. - Backpressure behavior: when buffer pressure is high, prefer local tail-drop of low-priority (debug) traces, emit a telemetry counter and increment tenant-level soft-quota. - Replay semantics: replay honors original trace order per-tenant within segments; provide a fast-path that can chunk by parent-request to speed up ingestion. - Security considerations: replay API is admin-only, authenticated via customer KMS-backed tokens; replay payloads must be validated against schema to prevent injection into downstream processors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector emits watermark token on all ingressed traces with tenant and seq-window fields populated. 2) On-disk buffer persists up to configured retention and survives collector restart. 3) Replay API replays traces preserving original timestamps and tenant attribution; downstream ingest shows matching trace IDs and no duplicates beyond allowable window. 4) Metrics exported: buffer_segments_total, buffer_occupancy_bytes, replay_success_total, replay_fail_total, tenant_replay_rate (per-tenant); dashboards in Console show per-tenant occupancy and replay history. 5) Security review completed and integration tests added to private-deploy e2e harness.

2025-01-23 - Tomás Ortega: Spike completed for append-only on-disk buffer; measured 22ms median write for 1KB trace payloads on m5.large equiv VM. Added compaction plan.
2025-01-28 - Design feedback (Ayesha Malik): suggested adding replay dry-run mode and CSV export for compliance teams; accepted and added to ACs.
2025-01-30 - Security review kickoff (Oliver Chen): noted replay API must rotate tokens and enforce MFA for manual replays; we will integrate with existing RBAC and KMS flow.

2025-02-02 - Engineering update (Tomás Ortega): implemented watermark header and integration tests with perimeter-forwarder shim; found duplicate suppression edge-case when tenant window hashes collide — mitigated by extending hash salt to include cluster-id.

2025-02-03 - QA (Lena Park): started safety tests for high-throughput replay (10k traces/min) and observed 1.2% replay_fail under constrained network; next step: add adaptive throttling on replay to honor downstream soft-quota.
